rationale: Record the snapshot-enabled receipt, resolve the registered gap and open an independent lead. Receipt fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 (all five tests passed) produced the same signature as the NoSnapshot run with an Entry whose Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true: the two re-synchronized followers ended at accepted 7 over six indices of content with read(5) None and a one-element decided read (events 51, 52) and the leader ended at accepted 6 with decided 7, is_reconfigured false and an unreadable decided log (event 53), against a baseline in which all three reported 6/6 with a six-element read (events 48-50). The interpretation now covers all five receipts, the knowledge conditions are re-stated for both entry configurations, and the gap that asked about the snapshot option and about a leader's own inflation is answered as resolved on both halves. A child question is registered for a different pairing in the same mechanism area - the adopted decided index and the adopted log come from different promises in handle_majority_promises - to be pursued next.

interpretations.rationale: Five receipts support one index-space confusion and three of its consequences, and the last one shows the defect is not tied to entry configuration. (1) A replica that already accepted the configuration's StopSign and receives a resume point that covers it ends one index past its content: for a follower re-synchronized after reconnected() (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35), for a follower that merely re-promised in a new term after an ordinary leader change with no reconnected() call (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), for the leader that took over from such a follower (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13), and for two followers under a snapshot-capable entry type (fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 51, 52: accepted 7 over six indices of content, read(5) None, one-element decided read). In every case the replica's own reconfiguration endpoint and decided-log read degrade. (2) A write quorum of inflated reports makes the leader decide the reported index although it holds fewer indices: the NoSnapshot case (event 24 of the first two receipts) and now the snapshot-enabled case (event 53: accepted 6, decided 7, is_reconfigured false, decided log unreadable), which is the same signature with both entry configurations. (3) The corruption propagates across authority changes: in the newterm/staleleader sequence the follower that re-promised was inflated (event 11) while the new leader and the cut-off node stayed at 6/6 (events 9, 10), and after the cut-off node took over it was itself inflated (event 13) with all three nodes at accepted 7 and a one-element decided read (events 12, 14). Controls held in every run: the pre-change samples (events 6-8, 48-50) and the no-reconnect control (events 9-11 of the first receipt) kept accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true and a six-element decided log for every replica. The registered gap is therefore answered on both halves: the leader-side inflation is witnessed and the snapshot option reproduces rather than avoids the inflation.
counterevidence: The no-reconnect control kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11), and in the newterm case the new leader and the node that received nothing stayed consistent (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 events 9, 10), so the deviation follows a re-synchronization whose resume point covers the StopSign rather than the reconfiguration or the harness.

The leader-side inflation witness is entangled with the propagation stage: when the cut-off node took over, all three nodes ended at accepted 7 with decided 7 and a one-element decided read (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea events 12-14), so that stage shows the leader's own accepted index exceeded its six indices of content but does not by itself separate its recomputation from the followers' later reports; the isolated single-replica cases (event 35 of the second receipt, event 11 of the third) are the clean witnesses of the resume-point effect.

The leader-side phantom decision requires a write quorum of inflated reporters in one term (two of three nodes); a single inflated follower, or one inflated follower plus a node that received nothing, left the leader consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9).

The documented reconfiguration flow (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true), which narrows the window in which a user reads the old instance, but the leader never observes the decision after the corruption and the followers keep reporting it while their decided log silently loses the entries.
limitations: Compaction itself (trim and snapshot calls) was not exercised; only the entry type's use_snapshots() flag differs in the snapshot-enabled run, where the snapshot branch of create_log_sync is evaluated but not entered.

Loss-triggered and timer-triggered re-synchronization were not exercised: messages were delivered in FIFO order without loss and no tick() timers ran, so the observed producers are explicit reconnected() calls and ordinary leader changes with one node cut off.

The consequence is bounded by the sealed configuration: after the StopSign is accepted no further entries can be accepted, so the phantom decided index carries no value and no value can be mis-assigned; the demonstrated effects are the corrupted index accounting, the unreadable or blank decided log and the lost reconfiguration endpoint rather than divergent values.

All three nodes used in-memory storage; persistence across a restart and other storages' behaviour on out-of-range reads (a storage-implementer responsibility per the Storage trait) were not exercised.
Only three-node clusters were exercised; larger clusters and repeated leader changes beyond the one newterm/staleleader sequence were not.

e40cd046de9e4f37b5761260b8dc599e-gap-2.explanation: Both halves are now settled. Leader half: witnessed - after the previously cut-off node took the lead from a follower whose Promise carried the StopSign, that leader reported accepted index 7 while holding six indices of content with read(5) None (receipt dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13), matching handle_majority_promises passing the follower's LogSync into sync_log (leader.rs 257-285, follower.rs 13-51). Snapshot half: witnessed - with an Entry whose Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true the two-follower reconnection after a decided StopSign produced the same states as the NoSnapshot case (receipt fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 51, 52 for the followers and 53 for the leader against the baseline at events 48-50), consistent with the source reading that the snapshot branch is not entered while the sender's decided index equals the resume point (mod.rs 405-432, internal_storage.rs 385-412, 469-474).

interpretations.joint_history: Five successive invocations of one harness lineage, read separately and never combined: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 (resync, control), 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 (plus single resync and a read of index 6), 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 (plus newterm), dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea (plus the staleleader stage) and fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 (plus a snapshot-capable entry type). Same three-node setup and public endpoints; each successor reproduces the earlier witnesses.

knowledge.assertion: sync_log double-counts the StopSign when the resumed prefix already covers it
a re-synchronized replica's decided log read loses the entries
the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index
the leader decides the reported accepted index without bounding it to its own log
a candidate leader syncing from a follower is inflated in its own accepted index

knowledge.statement: InternalStorage::sync_log sets accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and, when LogSync.stopsign is Some, adds one further index for that StopSign before returning; it does not subtract the LogSync's prefix, so when sync_idx already addresses the StopSign's own index the replica's accepted index ends up one larger than the entries it holds. SequencePaxos::create_log_sync does not adjust sync_idx for a StopSign already present on the sender: it uses its caller's common_prefix_idx unchanged and attaches the sender's stored StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Reached when a replica applies an AcceptSync or a leader applies a Promise whose LogSync carries stopsign = Some; the accounting is unconditional with respect to whether the resumed prefix already contained a StopSign. Exercised in five receipts: two reconnected followers ended at accepted 7 over six indices of content (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 22, 23), one reconnected follower did the same (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35), a follower that merely re-promised in a new term did the same (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), the leader that synced from it did the same (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13), and the same pattern occurred with a snapshot-capable entry type (fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 51-53), while pre-change samples and the no-reconnect control stayed at 6/6 with a six-element decided read.

knowledge.statement: On a replica that already holds the accepted StopSign, applying an AcceptSync whose LogSync carries that StopSign leaves the stored log unchanged while the reported accepted index rises by one; the replica's read of the StopSign's previous index (5) then returns None, its read of index 6 returns the StopSign, and read_decided_suffix(0) returns a decided log that omits the five entries: one element (the StopSign) when the replica's decided index has been pushed past that index, and an empty list when its decided index still stops there.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster, five decided entries plus a StopSign, default batch size, the re-synchronized replica having already accepted the StopSign. Observed for both entry configurations (Snapshot::use_snapshots() false in receipts 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8/9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63/6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789, true in fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5) and for both producers (reconnected() and an ordinary leader change), with the decided-log read reduced to one element or nothing against six elements before.

knowledge.statement: The inflated accepted index follows from the resume point being compared against the index the StopSign occupies in the receiving replica's accounting: sync_log computes accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and adds one for a carried StopSign, while the StopSign occupies the index accepted_idx - 1 and the sender attaches it without shifting sync_idx. The condition is therefore sync_idx + suffix.len() >= the StopSign's index, and it does not depend on the snapshot option: the no-snapshot branch passes the caller's common_prefix_idx unchanged (a re-promising follower's accepted index, or a candidate leader's decided index), whereas the snapshot branch passes the compacted index returned by create_diff_snapshot, which is derived from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign and therefore excludes the StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Holds for any LogSync whose stopsign is Some. Observed producer instances: a follower re-synchronized after reconnected() at the same ballot (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63), a follower re-presenting its accepted index when it re-promises in a new term after an ordinary leader change (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), and a candidate leader that syncs from such a follower (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13). The snapshot option was exercised directly with a snapshot-capable entry type: the same inflation appeared (fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 51-53), consistent with the snapshot branch not being entered while the sender's decided index equals the resume point.

investigations.question: When a leader is elected, does it hold the entries up to the decided index it adopts from its read quorum? handle_majority_promises takes the maximum decided index over all promises but the log itself from the single maximum promise metadata, so a promise that reports a decided index covering more entries than that maximum's log could make the adopted decided index exceed the entries the leader holds.
investigations.hypothesis: The adopted decided index can exceed the leader's accepted index whenever the promise with the maximum decided index is not the promise whose log_sync the leader adopts with it (different (n_accepted, accepted_idx) ordering than decided_idx), because sync_log sets the decided index and the log from two independent inputs.
investigations.discriminator: Sample a newly elected leader's decided index against its accepted index and its readable decided log right after its prepare phase, in a history where one promise reports the higher decided index while another promise supplies the log_sync (for example a follower that accepted the StopSign under a later round but reports fewer entries than a promise that decided it).
